text.p: German first division programme this weekend:
Difficult match for the leaders but they should be at full strength. Promoted Bochum have not lost at home this season although Bayer have a good away record.

Bremen are without suspended Austrian playmaker Andreas Herzog. Both teams need a win after poor runs. Bremen have not won any of their last five matches. 1860s run without a victory is one match longer.
Karlsruhe need to put disappointing UEFA Cup exit behind them. Bottom club Freiburg have conceded more goals than any other team and have just one point from last three games.
Schalke have psychological boost of UEFA Cup quarter-final place but are without suspended Czech midfielder Radoslav Latal. Schalke enjoying good run, taking nine points from last three games.
Hamburg's season further deteriorated after midweek UEFA Cup exit by Monaco. Home side looking for points after failing to win any of last four games.
Stuttgart missing Germany's Euro 96 striker Fredi Bobic (suspended) and midfielder Gerhard Poschner (suspended). Promoted Bielefeld struggled for most of first half of the season but improving.

Bayern without defender-cum-libero Thomas Helmer who has just undergone gallstone operation and goalkeeper Oliver Kahn doubtful with groin injury. Lothar Matthaeus to return to libero role from midfield. Bayern not lost at home this season. Moenchengladbach failed to win any of last five games.
Middle-of-table clash which should be tight game. Duisburg have improved last few games but St Pauli also unbeaten in last three matches.

Cologne finally making championship challenge after disappointing last few seasons but European Cup quarter-finalists Dortmund are unbeaten in last seven games and one of the league's best away teams.
